    • Sources indicate that AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants.
    • Sources indicate that according to ShellBench, a fresh benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time.
    • ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that AI companies have spent the last couple of months marketing personal AI agents as tools to take over the digital drudgery of human existence — and millions have been sold on the vision, handing over their shopping schedules, travel plans, and everyday responsibilities to AI assistants. But upcoming research suggests that even the most advanced AI models struggle to reliably and safely navigate the messy details of people’s lives.

    Sources indicate that according to ShellBench, a fresh benchmark for everyday agent work, even the most advanced models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta failed more than a third of the time. Across all models tested, 15.7% of attempts failed at least one safety requirement, often leading to unintended consequences.

    ShellBench was developed in collaboration with researchers at The OpenClaw Foundation, Parsewave, Hugging Face, Red Hat, and UC Berkeley, drawing on more than 10 million anonymized, real-world AI agent interactions to see how agents perform on the everyday work people actually delegate to them.

    The research comes as personal AI assistants are finding newly introduced popularity among developers, with Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic all fighting for a piece of the market with Muse, Dots, and Claude Duet, respectively.

    It has been revealed that in October, Meta noted more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up its personal AI agent, Muse, within six weeks of launch, with about a quarter using it daily. That number is expected to grow as Meta implants Muse directly into Instagram DMs. Despite growing popularity among consumers, we still have little evidence about how reliable AI personal assistant products actually are.

    ShellBench suggests that the unreliable nature of most everyday data sources still causes problems for many state-of-the-art systems. A successful agent should be able to navigate messy personal workspaces containing emails, calendar entries, spreadsheets, receipts, chat logs, outdated information, and phishing attempts, and figure out which information is relevant, what is private, and how to deliver the requested outcome without creating new problems.

    It seems many of today’s AI agents are still not up to the task. Not only did even the highest-performing agents frequently fail to meet the requirements of a task, but they also lacked consistency. When researchers ran each task three times under identical conditions, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra, the highest-scoring model, nailed all three attempts less than half the time.

    For autonomous assistants that are meant to run in the background without supervision, it’s a problem if people need to run an agent multiple times to get a result they trust.

    Recent findings suggest that additionally, about 10% of otherwise correct attempts failed at least one safety criterion. Across the models and harnesses tested, agents failed to, for example, adequately account for a child’s school pickup 79.5% of the time. When handling laptop custody records, agents failed a requirement to identify and withhold a sensitive bank upload token in 18.6% of attempts. In another task, agents recommended duplicate or incorrect invoice payments 40.3% of the time.

    The findings highlight a major problem for consumers adopting consumer personal AI assistants, namely that there’s always a risk that an agent can create more headaches in the course of trying to fulfill an otherwise ordinary request.

    While AI benchmarks have largely focused on coding, professional work, or testing on specific tasks, ShellBench is attempting to evaluate how models perform on multi-step personal tasks within different agent harnesses — the software that controls how a model accesses information, uses tools, and takes actions.

    While the researchers found model choice had a greater overall impact on performance than harness choice, among the more capable models, AI agent performance became more dependent on the harness.

    For example, OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra outperformed Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 when operating within the Pi harness, but it performed worse when both models were tested within Claude Code.

    Sources indicate that meta’s Muse Wonder Full scored 56% in Pi, but only 38.1% in Claude Code. Meta’s Muse Wonder 1.0, meanwhile, averaged a success rate of 39.7% across the five harnesses tested.

    Notably, while the researchers tested models from Meta, OpenAI, and Anthropic, they didn’t evaluate them within the native harnesses of Muse, Dots, or Claude Duet, so the results may not be representative of the experience millions of consumers are having with the product today.

    TechCrunch has reached out to Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, and the researchers in the study.

    #105151. Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical concerns

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1010 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Half of NASA's aging Mars fleet knocked offline by technical concerns

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1010 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Two of NASA’s four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks.
    • It has been revealed that the missions affected by the outages—hopefully temporary—are NASA’s Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter.
    • The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover’s communications system.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Two of NASA’s four missions operating at Mars have suspended science operations after encountering separate technical issues in recent weeks.

    It has been revealed that the missions affected by the outages—hopefully temporary—are NASA’s Perseverance rover and Odyssey orbiter. Both are operating beyond their original design lifetimes. Perseverance is in its sixth year exploring the surface of Mars, having collected rock and soil samples for eventual return to Earth. The rover is now studying the rim of a crater that once contained an ancient lake of liquid water. Odyssey arrived in orbit around Mars in 2001, and is the longest-lived Mars mission in history.

    The problem on Perseverance stems from the rover’s communications system. The rover has two redundant UHF radios for high-rate communications with a fleet of orbiters that relay data to Earth. A separate X-band system is available for direct-to-Earth communications at a lower data rate.

    One of the rover’s two UHF radios was unresponsive when it powered up on October 30, triggering an automatic switch to the backup radio and placing the rover in safe mode. Ground teams at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California later discovered the backup UHF radio was transmitting at about half of its expected power output, NASA mentioned in a statement last week.

    “The team has stopped using both radios until they can evaluate potential causes of the complications and one or both are deemed safe to resume operating,” NASA remarked.

    Industry observers note that perseverance is now transmitting signals directly to Earth in X-band, but the connection provides a “significantly lower data rate” than relaying signals through orbiters using the UHF radios. Mission managers paused the rover’s science operations “out of an abundance of caution” as they investigate the radio problem. Their initial focus is on getting the backup UHF radio running before turning their attention on recovering the primary radio, NASA remarked.

    “The team is hopeful the rover could return to science by the end of November.”.

    Sources indicate that the six-wheeled robot broke a record last month for the farthest any vehicle has driven on another planet. The Perseverance rover surpassed the 28.06-mile (45.16-kilometer) mark set by NASA’s Opportunity rover, which stopped working in 2018. Perseverance’s odometer now sits at twice the rover’s original goal for distance traveled.

    Sources indicate that the situation with the Odyssey orbiter seems more dire. One of the four reaction wheels used for pointing the spacecraft stopped spinning in early November, leaving Odyssey with two good wheels after the first one failed in 2013. The orbiter needs at least three wheels to keep it oriented correctly.

    “Without the three reaction wheels, the spacecraft must rely solely on its hydrazine thrusters to remain oriented,” NASA mentioned. The orbiter requires stable pointing to turn its solar arrays toward the Sun and its science instruments toward Mars.

    Odyssey was running low on propellant before the reaction wheel malfunction, but managers were optimistic that with “extremely low” fuel usage, the orbiter would have enough to continue operating through at least the end of 2028, noted Jeffrey Plaut, Odyssey’s project scientist at JPL, in a presentation earlier this year.

    That assumed no failures in Odyssey’s three remaining reaction wheels. Without three healthy wheels, engineers estimate the spacecraft has enough hydrazine fuel to last one to two months, NASA stated. The good news is ground teams had some initial success troubleshooting the balky reaction wheel. Further testing is necessary to determine whether the wheel is recoverable.

    Recent findings suggest that odyssey is one of four orbiters NASA uses to relay data between Earth and the Perseverance and Curiosity rovers on the Martian surface. Curiosity is still driving and collecting data after 14 years on Mars. The other three relay craft are NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, which reached the red planet in 2006, the European Space Agency’s 10-year-old ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter, and ESA’s 23-year-old Mars Express spacecraft.

    According to recent reports, NASA lost contact with its MAVEN orbiter last December after 11 years of operations at Mars when the spacecraft suddenly spun out of control. An investigation could not identify a specific root cause, but engineers concluded that a radiation-induced single event upset or a software matter caused MAVEN’s flight computer to reboot, according to Tiffany Morgan, director of NASA’s robotic Mars Exploration Program.

    The spacecraft’s inertial measurement unit failed to provide the computer with correct information on MAVEN’s orientation, causing it to spin in response to the faulty data, Morgan said in a November 9 presentation to the Mars Exploration Program Analysis Group.

    NASA is preparing to send reinforcements to renew the agency’s presence at Mars. In September, NASA awarded Blue Origin a $700 million contract for the Mars Telecommunications Network (MTN), an orbiter dedicated to providing high-bandwidth connectivity between Earth and other missions operating on and around the red planet.

    It has been revealed that NASA wanted Blue Origin to complete the telecom orbiter by the end of 2028 and have it operational at Mars in 2030. But the Mars Telecommunications Network is on hold after Rocket Lab, which lost its bid to win the MTN contract, filed a protest with the Government Accountability Office. The GAO is expected to rule on the protest next month, at which time Blue Origin could start work on the NASA contract if the government rejects Rocket Lab’s petition.

    Another Mars mission, SkyFall, could also launch in 2028. NASA aims to send three helicopter drones to Mars to explore the planet’s geology and weather from the air.

    A perennial priority for Mars scientists is replacing the unique high-resolution mapping camera on the aging Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter. Such a capability will help identify landing sites for future robotic and human missions, including a potential mission to return Perseverance’s rock specimens to Earth.

    It has been revealed that NASA is in the very early stages of developing a mission concept that could take over MRO’s imaging capability, but there’s no firm schedule or budget for such an undertaking. NASA will likely rely on MRO for landing-site reconnaissance well into the 2030s.

    Change this Roku TV setting to watch movies how they were filmed

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (381 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • You don't have to leave your TV's refresh rate at 60fps.
    • Recent findings suggest that if you were to travel back in time thirty years and show someone a smart TV from today, their head would likely explode.
    • Buried deep in your Roku TV's settings is a way to alter the refresh rate, and there's a very specific reason that you might want to do that.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    You don't have to leave your TV's refresh rate at 60fps.

    Recent findings suggest that if you were to travel back in time thirty years and show someone a smart TV from today, their head would likely explode. In addition to the seemingly limitless amount of content one can find and interact with on a modern television, your Roku TV also may have the ability to let you watch movies in a far more compelling way.

    Buried deep in your Roku TV's settings is a way to alter the refresh rate, and there's a very specific reason that you might want to do that. Most Roku TVs default to a refresh rate of 60fps. While that's going to be perfectly fine for some situations, it doesn't make for the most theatrical viewing experience — for the most part, movies are filmed and projected at 24fps. It's the standard, and it has defined the way movies look and feel for decades. When you go to the movie theater, you're watching a 24fps output.

    Roku allows you to alter your TV's refresh rate to match that, offering something a bit closer to the original intent of those films.

    According to recent reports, there are a lot of ways to change the overall look and display of your Roku TV, but most of that discourse seems centered around colors and contrast. Those things are crucial, but if you really want to achieve a "movie look," then you'll want to change the refresh rate.

    In your Roku TV, to match this unique look, you'll need to first go to the main menu. From here, select Settings, and then go into System. In this menu, you'll find something called Advanced System Settings, which will allow you to access Advanced Display Settings. You want to turn Auto-adjust display refresh rate on.

    It's a one-click and done solution, as it will self-adjust itself to match the native refresh rate of any movie or TV show you put on. Because films have a native refresh rate of 24fps, your TV will now run them as such. The same goes for TV shows, which may be filmed at 30 or 60fps. It's a tiny adjustment, but it's one that will make your viewing experience even better.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Watch: India's government is 'scared', cockroach movement leader says after travel ban.
    • One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has stated the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.
    • Saurav Das said he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Watch: India's government is 'scared', cockroach movement leader says after travel ban.

    One of the leaders of India's "cockroach" movement has stated the Delhi government has "completely lost the plot" after he was stopped from leaving the country for the UK.

    Saurav Das said he was meant to board a flight on Tuesday morning but was told by immigration officers his passport had been "flagged" because of discrepancies involving his date of birth.

    In an interview with the BBC, Das said there were no discrepancies in his documents, accusing the Indian government of using cheap tactics to stop activists from travelling and speaking on complications that matter to young people.

    The BBC has reached out to the federal home ministry, Delhi police and airport officials for comment.

    Saurav told the BBC World Service's Newshour programme the incident showed the government was "scared".

    Industry observers note that "They are scared of the cockroach movement. They're scared of young people asking them questions because they have never had to deal with a generation that wants to ask questions so head on. So that jitters them.".

    By not allowing him to travel, he remarked the government had lowered India's stature in the world.

    Recent findings suggest that "It's international news that I am unable to travel to the UK," he said. "And this shows Prime Minister Modi in such poor light.

    "It's a way to harass, to target activists, young voices in India by the Modi government.".

    Das noted he had been invited by the Oxford Union, as well as universities including Cambridge and Edinburgh, to speak about the movement.

    Ratna Singh, another leader of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), wrote: "The manner in which Saurav was not allowed to board today raises deeply troubling questions about the state of freedom of expression and the space being allowed for young voices in this country.".

    On Tuesday, the London School of Economics Student Union's Amnesty International Unit, a student-led charity group, shared a post on Instagram saying that an event featuring Das had been "indefinitely postponed".

    Saurav Das (L) speaking following the resignation of India's education minister in July.

    Das, a former journalist, became one of the faces of the CJP - a Gen Z-led movement that began as satire but has since emerged as a youth-led pressure group.

    In July, protests spearheaded by the CJP over exam paper leaks led to the resignation of India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan .

    In October, CJP leaders including Das were among thousands detained by the police for trying to hold protests demanding the resignation of India's Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. Kumar and the Election Commission have denied wrongdoing.

    The same month, Das and Ashutosh Ranka, another CJP leader, were jailed for seven days after being arrested for trespassing at a banned protest site in Delhi.

    Das insisted the CJP would continue protesting, but it did not want to be a political party "as of today".

    "It's a long haul. We are not here for a short time. We are looking at India in the next 10 to 20 years. How do we develop India into a better country? That is the vision that we want to carry forward.".

    Abhijeet Dipke, the founder of CJP, wrote on X that if Das "had looted a bank or committed financial fraud", he may have been allowed to fly to London, referring to billionaire bank-loan defaulters who have left India.

    There have been other instances in recent years of people being prevented from boarding flights.

    In September 2025, Bhanu Tatak, an environmental and anti-dam activist from India's north-eastern Arunachal Pradesh state, was stopped from boarding a flight to Dublin.

    Recent findings suggest that in March 2022, Rana Ayyub, an investigative journalist and outspoken critic of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government, was also stopped from boarding a flight to London at the Mumbai airport. She was due to speak at different events on media freedom and the targeting of journalists.

    Additional reporting by Cherylann Mollan.

    Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.

    Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one massive effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.

    It has been revealed that leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.

    PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running.

    Sources indicate that at this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    After a whirlwind period during which Jensen Huang’s life fell apart and then came back together again, the Nvidia founder now wants his staff to know that he’s a changed man.

    Huang held Nvidia’s first all-hands meeting on Tuesday since his reinstatement on Monday. During that meeting, CNBC reported that Huang struck a “remorseful tone” and told the crowd “I hurt all of you.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the founder, whose extramarital affairs have been accused of jeopardizing everything from the stock market to U.S. national security, went on to describe how difficult the current moment is for him: “This is going to be the hardest tech giant meeting I’ve ever done, and the second hardest meeting I have ever done,” Huang reportedly told staff.

    “The hardest meeting I’ve ever done was with my wife,” he added.

    The CEO admitted in the meeting that he had flouted Nvidia’s code of conduct, which he himself had largely devised. Huang emphasized that the code of conduct was still in effect, but that mitigating circumstances would matter a lot. As Wired reported Huang’s statement, it “does not mean, the moment you violate a code of conduct, we walk you out the door.”.

    Huang told staff that he’s in therapy and also said that he was grateful for a second chance at the manufacturer.

    It has been revealed that the CEO is now walking a difficult tight rope between reasserting his authority over one of the world’s most powerful and influential companies, and conceding that he may have made some mistakes. He also tackled the difficult question of President Trump’s role in his restoration. The president reportedly called Nvidia’s board directly to lobby for Huang’s return, but in his talk, Huang downplayed Trump’s role.

    Huang thanked the administration on Tuesday for “providing Nvidia with quick access to intelligence that he said helped the board determine that the national security risks the organization faced in reinstating him were low,” The Wall Street Journal writes.

    Industry observers note that huang will likely need the administration’s support as he weathers an upcoming wave of congressional scrutiny from a newly Democrat-led government. The CEO is scheduled to appear for a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week and, in the coming weeks, he will be called to appear for a number of different closed House hearings, including for the Intelligence Committee, the Foreign Affairs Committee, and the China Select Committee.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.

    The Chinese telecom giant was also found guilty of bank fraud.

    A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, as reported earlier by NBC News and Bloomberg. The verdict, handed down in a federal court in Latest York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile, Cisco, and Motorola.

    The Department of Justice’s 2018 criminal indictment against Huawei came to light following the arrest of the company’s CFO, Wanzhou Meng, whom the agency accused of fraud. Though the indictment against Meng was eventually dismissed, she admitted to misleading banks over Huawei’s operations in Iran as part of a deferred prosecution agreement. The US government blacklisted Huawei in 2019 over national security concerns.

    In total, the jury found Huawei guilty of 10 of 12 criminal counts, including money laundering, violating US sanctions, bank fraud, wire fraud, and conspiracy to defraud the US. The organization was acquitted of engaging in a criminal racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. Huawei’s sentencing is set for September 14th, 2027, where it may face “financial penalties including criminal fines, forfeiture, and restitution,” according to the DOJ.

    It has been revealed that “For over two decades, Huawei built its global empire on a foundation of fraud, theft, and deception,” Tysen A. Duva, the assistant attorney general of the DOJ’s criminal division, claims in a statement. “Huawei’s crimes threatened the U.S. financial system, took advantage of American companies that compete honestly in the global telecommunications market, and undermined our national security.”.

    In a statement to NBC News, a Huawei spokesperson said the charges are “without legal or factual merit” and that it plans to appeal the decision. Huawei didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

    Update, November 24th: Added information from the DOJ.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang kicked off his return to the chipmaker he co-founded by holding an all-hands meeting that covered remorse, therapy, and even the manufacturer’s code of conduct, according to accounts from multiple insiders who spoke to the media.

    Sources indicate that the topic of succession planning also came up — a particularly sticky concern seen as a key risk at Nvidia. Huang reportedly told staff that Nvidia doesn’t require succession planning because of its unique business model, CNBC reported, citing an unnamed source who was present. Surprisingly, given the events of the last two weeks, Huang argued that a succession plan would create unnecessary hierarchy.

    Industry observers note that investors and analysts saw the problem differently earlier this month, when Huang resigned as CEO following his admission that he had extramarital affairs with at least two people, including one whom the U.S. government suspects of being a Chinese spy.

    Recent findings suggest that nvidia is a flat organization, unlike other large corporations that have a swath of C-suite executives and multiple layers of management. Huang sits at the top and notes he has about 60 direct reports. Nvidia has just five executive officers running the show, including Huang. The other four are CFO Colette Kress, who was interim CEO for 12 days; Ajay Puri, who heads worldwide field operations; Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations; and Timothy Teter, executive vice president and general counsel, according to the company’s regulatory filings.

    Huang has previously defended the organization’s structure in numerous interviews, including one in March with podcaster Lex Fridman.

    Sources indicate that “When you’re designing a firm, you should first think about what is it that you want the company to produce,” Huang remarked in the interview. “You know, I see a lot of companies’ organization charts, and they all look the same. Hamburger [company] organization charts, software organization charts, and car company organization charts. They all look the same. And it doesn’t make any sense to me. You know, the goal of company is to be the machinery, the mechanism, the system that produces the output. And that output is the product that we like to create.”.

    Huang’s comments to staff, and his previous remarks on the topic of succession, may not be enough to assuage the board or shareholders over the long term, however.

    Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi.

    The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially mentioned he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy.

    Sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars. He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday.

    Since losing his re-election bid in 2012, Sarkozy has faced several criminal investigations.

    In 2024, he was handed a one-year sentence â of which six months were suspended â over the illegal financing of his 2012 re-election campaign.

    According to recent reports, in 2021, he was found guilty of trying to bribe a judge and sentenced to three years in jail â two of them suspended â and thus became the first former French president to get a custodial sentence. He was allowed to serve his time at home wearing a tag instead of going to jail.

    The upcoming case centres on a Libyan businessman, Ziad Takieddine, who had said he had written proof that Sarkozy's 2007 campaign bid was "abundantly" financed by Tripoli, and that the â¬50m (Â£43m) in payments continued after he became president.

    Takieddine, who died last year, withdrew his accusations in an interview in 2020.

    At the time, Sarkozy was stated to have stated: the "truth is finally coming out", but officials found the retraction to be "insincere" and a fresh investigation was released into the "Save Sarko" file â the nickname the alleged perpetrators had used for the operation, according to French media.

    Industry observers note that so the former head of state and his wife, an Italian-born former supermodel and singer, will now face charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" and benefiting from witness tampering. They deny any wrongdoing.

    #105126. Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa

    📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1278 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 The Verge ↗ Open Full Page

    Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa

    📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1278 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: The Verge

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.
    • The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.
    • The US Army is moving ahead with intends to detonate the nation’s stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.

    The US Army is scrambling to contain any potential lead pollution that could spread if an old stockpile of explosives blows up.

    The US Army is moving ahead with intends to detonate the nation’s stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday. The Verge reached out to experts on what to expect, and will keep this post updated.

    What material is the Army planning to detonate?

    Industry observers note that there are 68 drums holding about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound created to detonate munitions like grenades. The US started using lead azide as a primary explosive almost a century ago before “moving away” from it about 15 years ago because of how difficult the material is to store and transport, Robert Cekada, director of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), said in a Tuesday press briefing. At that point, the US transferred its remaining stockpile of lead azide to the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown. Lead azide will explode at 350 degrees Celsius (662F). But it is also sensitive to flame, friction, or sudden shock, including fluctuations in temperature.

    Some of the material on site in Iowa is more than 60 years old. The material can crystallize as it degrades over time, becoming unstable enough to explode even at ambient temperatures. The Army noted some deterioration of the material in 2009 — but not any “dangerous crystallization” at the time, according to Cekada.

    “It’s not a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.”.

    According to recent reports, the chemical was stored in liquid form, embedded in sawdust and burlap bags inside the drums. Water and ethanol were also added to the containers to keep the lead azide from freezing in the winter. But during a March inspection, Cekada noted ATF noticed “significant crystallization on the exterior of the barrels.” That made the material too unstable for them to open the barrels to add more water and ethanol, Cekada said. Removing a lid might cause the barrels to detonate.

    Why is the Army detonating it now?

    Industry observers note that officials have been trying to figure out what to do with the crystallized lead azide since that alarming March inspection. The Army initially hired a contractor to safely dissolve the chemicals but canceled the contract earlier this year, according to reporting by The New York Times. Using a chemical neutralization agent “proved to be an unsafe method,” Army Col. Aaron Teller, commander of the 71st Explosive Ordinance Disposal Group, said at the Tuesday briefing, because crystallization on the outside of the barrels made it too risky to open the lids.

    According to recent reports, “Everyone that we’ve spoken to through their experience has determined that this is the only safe path forward,“ Cekada said at the briefing. If they leave the chemicals as is, he said, they’re still at risk of exploding. “It’s not a matter of if, it’s a matter of when.”.

    Compared to an uncontrolled, spontaneous explosion, a controlled detonation is supposed to limit the amount of lead dust unleashed on surrounding communities and the environment. Still, the dust plume could reach as far as 100 miles away from the site. The Army has released maps showing where lead dust is expected to travel based on its modeling.

    The last time the Army disposed of lead azide this way at a comparable scale was in 1977, according to Teller. At the time, they detonated 7,000 pounds of the material in Colorado in open air “with zero mitigation.” Even then, 75 percent of the lead particulate stayed on site, Teller remarked at the briefing. The Army now believes it can “significantly reduce” the spread of that last 25 percent of lead using walls made up of four 16,000-gallon water tanks to capture lead particulate and hopefully prevent it from escaping into the atmosphere.

    Industry observers note that the 80-year-old earth-covered magazines holding the lead azide are cracked and deteriorating, Teller noted, and they are likely to break open after the detonation. To prepare, they’ve covered it with tarp and a special containment screen for lead. They also plan to flood it with 2 feet of foam to capture particulate pollution. Adam Telle, Acting Secretary of the Army, also noted the Army has set out “state of the art gel blocks in huge quantities all around to ensure that we absorb as much of this blast as we possibly can.”.

    There is no “safe” level of exposure to lead.

    Last week, the Iowa Environmental Council and Sierra Club sought a court order to stop the explosion from taking place, pending an Environmental and Health Impact Statement and an investigation into alternatives to detonating the material. President Donald Trump chimed in on social media, calling for a pause until a federal appeals court gave the Army the green light after previously granting a temporary stay. The court on Monday denied the emergency motion to stop the explosion, clearing the way for the Army to move forward.

    What precautions can people nearby take?

    According to recent reports, the Iowa Department of Health and Human Services (Iowa HHS) recommends that anyone in potentially affected areas stay indoors and keep windows shut for 24 to 48 hours after the detonation. Iowa HHS also suggests switching off HVAC systems that might bring outdoor air inside or set them to modes that recirculate air, and using an air purifier with a HEPA filter.

    In a recent development, FEMA is helping relocate Middletown residents and others within a voluntary 5-mile evacuation zone. People who are pregnant, children, and individuals with chronic diseases should evacuate the affected areas, Sean Kaufman, principal deputy assistant secretary for preparedness and response at the Administration for Strategic Preparedness and Response, remarked at the briefing. “Outside of that area, if you’re close to that proximity and you’re uncomfortable, I think you need to do what you need to do to take care of your family,” Kaufman said.

    Industry observers note that there is no “safe” level of exposure to lead, a neurotoxin that poses health risks when inhaled or ingested. Kids are at increased risk because their brains are still developing and are also more likely to touch contaminated surfaces and then stick their fingers in their mouths. But most adverse health effects — which can include fatigue and gastrointestinal upset alongside impacts on brain development — are connected to chronic lead exposure rather than as a result of a one-off event.

    In a recent development, “It is likely this exposure will not result in any observable acute clinical signs,” Will Sander, associate professor of preventive medicine and public health at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, says in an email to The Verge. “Overall, the risk is minimal, and there should be no long-term concerns.”.

    What happens after the explosion?

    “The Army has done this before a long time ago and took lead measurements afterward that were low but hazardous (in my opinion),” Chris Kohler, an adjunct instructor at Indiana University who is an expert on hazardous waste, environmental remediation, and chemical hygiene, says in an email to The Verge. “The detonation will spread lead in the atmosphere. Not a desirable outcome.” Kohler and other experts say it’ll be important to continue monitoring the explosion site and surrounding areas to see if there needs to be any more remediation.

    US attorney general dodges questions about Nvidia investigation

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • How Nvidia is reacting to Jensen Huang's return as CEO.
    • US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.
    • Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    How Nvidia is reacting to Jensen Huang's return as CEO.

    US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.

    Blanche said he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.

    Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

    Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about.".

    Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia.

    The US commerce department has also declared it was preparing to blacklist the tech company Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China.

    In a joint statement last week, the commerce and justice departments mentioned they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".

    But speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Blanche mentioned the latter department has "hundreds, if not more" export investigations occurring at any one time.

    "So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he said.

    Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with any efforts to get to the bottom of whether the company or Huang potentially knew about any chips being diverted to China, Blanche said: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.

    "Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people.

    "It shouldn't be what my message would be either.".

    While Nvidia's stock market value surged on the announcement of Huang's reappointment, some of the gains were reversed in volatile Tuesday trading.

    Sources indicate that the firm's share price closed down nearly 6% - still well above where it ended last week. On Monday, Nvidia stock rocketed more than 31% following news of Huang's return.

    Faisal Islam: Fears over the AI boom haven't gone away.

    Industry observers note that the manufacturer's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, said Huang's return was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".

    The board stated it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.

    On Monday, Trump mentioned he spoke to the company's directors and convinced them to bring back Huang.

    Huang's reinstatement provoked bipartisan anger.

    Republican congressman Don Bacon mentioned Nvidia should have "ignored the Administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang".

    Republican Senator Pete Ricketts stated Huang's behaviour "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips".

    Democratic congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House oversight committee, said Trump's "direct involvement" with Nvidia's decision "raises serious national security and corruption questions".

    Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego said Congress needed to "investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement".

    During an interview with the Newly introduced York Post on Tuesday, President Trump remarked that pardoning Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has been ensnared in a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy, is “an option,” albeit one that he doesn’t think he will have to exercise.

    “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary,” the president reportedly told the outlet.

    Industry observers note that huang, who was ousted from his own tech giant less than two weeks ago, was reinstated Monday. He faces ongoing questions about his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence who previously worked for a company that has been accused of illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China.

    Huang is scheduled to testify at a public Senate Banking Committee hearing next week.

    When asked about the hearing, Trump reportedly said: “I think I want him to just tell the truth, and I mean, his lawyers are going to have to advise him, but I’ve always found him to be 100% aboveboard, and you know a very smart person.”.

    Recent findings suggest that at another point in the interview, when asked what he knew about Huang’s other extramarital affairs, Trump reportedly said: “I really didn’t get into that. I got into the business of chips, much more than the business of sex.”.

    TechCrunch has reached out to the White House for comment.

    Gone are the days when you could just buy your father a random tie or some leather-clad alcohol vessel or a shaving kit. Dads want — nay, deserve — something memorable. Luckily for you, it’s not that hard to find something special that he’ll approve of, and we’re here to guide you.

    Recent findings suggest that we’ve curated this year’s gift list with the modern father in mind, whether he’s a gamer, creator, chef, or simply a gadget lover. There’s a lot in here we think he’ll like, from noise-canceling headphones like the Sonos Ace Ultra and an autonomous drone to a brilliant QD-OLED monitor and a nifty light that’s perfect for illuminating his next campsite. Whatever your dad is into, we’ve got you covered.

    Industry observers note that cleaning gadgets like Dyson’s PencilVac FluffyCones are never cheap, but they’re often worth the cost and a pleasure to use. The lightweight, broom-replacing stick vacuum doesn’t do carpets, but its rolling bars pack incredible cleaning power for touching up hard floors, including stairs.

    Sources indicate that give the gift that fixes past home improvement transgressions. These handy Japanese-made pliers from Vampire Tools have one fundamental purpose — to remove stripped screws — and they’re damn good at it. The best part? Watching Dad’s face light up seconds before he sprints to the garage for them.

    Who would have thought a simple hook could make roaming the city with a backpack so much more convenient? After testing Peak Design’s well-designed bags, we’re convinced the clever addition is a game-changer for anyone who doesn’t want to leave their bag on the filthy ground.

    According to recent reports, give your father a little nostalgia and a lot of convenience in one package with this stylish USB-C dock and SSD combo gadget. The cassette-shaped Sharge Disk Pro 2 works as a hub with support for HDMI at 4K, SD and microSD card slots, USB-A and USB-C ports, along with up to 8TB of storage stored within.

    It’s time to help Dad ditch his collection of plastic reusable cups, which have clearly seen better days. NotNeutral’s hand-pressed, timeless tumbler offers ’70s vibes with a modern twist, making it the perfect vessel for whatever Dad twists into his favorite drink.

    Sources indicate that for those who love travel but hate the constraints of a hotel TV, Belkin’s ConnectAir is a slick solution. Plug the transmitter into any device with a USB-C video-out port and the receiver into the TV’s HDMI port, and voilà, you’re easily (and wirelessly) connected.

    Have you broken something fragile that seems impossible to mend? Maybe all you need is a Kintsugi Repair Kit, which provides the Japanese method and a special lacquer to repair and restore broken ceramics to good health. The resulting golden scar is merely to remind us that rebuilding is possible.

    According to recent reports, werewolf’s affordable dongle kit provides an almost magical way to power nearly any DC device from a USB-C charger or portable battery. Program it from a mobile app, connect it to your old gear, and everything from a PC monitor to an original Game Boy can accept USB-C charging.

    In a recent development, if your father already owns an Apple Watch, the Nomad Stratos is a foolproof upgrade idea. The refined watch band features titanium links with a rubbery interior for durable comfort, and it comes in an array of subtle color options that make it as suitable for the office as it is for the slopes.

    If you’re after a cheap, useful stocking stuffer, Trond’s reliable three-prong extension cord is a practical pick that’s available in leftward or rightward configurations to fit nearly any outlet. Dad will probably say, “Oh, I’ve always wanted one of these,” and this time he’ll mean it.

    Sources indicate that the CS-Pro will make your dad feel like a private eye in the early ’80s. The retro-inspired digital camera serves up 16-megapixel stills and offers four filters accessible from its tactile dial, plus USB-C charging, a high-quality Xenon flash, and a 4GB SD card for plenty of vintage photo fun.

    Antigravity’s A1 is the ultimate gadget for the dad who dreams of owning the sky. The compact drone comes with specialized goggles that will make him feel like he’s in the cockpit, and it records always-on, 360-degree 8K video. It’s an exhilarating flight experience and an excellent creator’s tool in one slick package.

    Sonos raised its headphones game on all fronts with the Ace Ultra, which deliver better noise canceling, improved sound, and the feature we’ve all been waiting for: Wi-Fi support. With the ability to bounce audio across your Sonos ecosystem, including from a TV via newer Sonos soundbars, Dad’s sonic sanctuary is finally complete.

    Industry observers note that wiiM’s first soundbar builds on its seamless Sonos-esque connectivity with a sleek design, detailed sound, and up-firing speakers for Dolby Atmos spatial audio. It also pairs with other speakers for surround sound through a no-fuss setup process, including ones you already own that are linked to one of WiiM’s amplifiers.

    It has been revealed that your dad needs an awesome monitor, but there are 10 billion options. Alienware’s 34-inch Penta Tandem QD-OLED delivers top-end picture quality, with vibrant colors and perfect blacks, plus a swift 280Hz refresh rate. Best of all, it’s not nearly as expensive as you might think.

    Recent findings suggest that if your dad is still reading books on his phone (or aging e-reader), it’s time for an upgrade. The latest in Amazon’s series of waterproof, auto-dimming e-readers loads books faster than the prior model and offers a slick aluminum upgrade. No matter which you choose, it’s a better way to bring the library along.

    It has been revealed that oura didn’t reinvent the wheel with the Ring 5, but it did reshape it into a slimmer, thinner, more wearable design that could make all the difference. Inside are the same extensive health and fitness tracking features for charting everything from sleep to heart health, backed by long battery life.

    Smart TVs are often pretty dumb. If your dad is always complaining about his TV, or if you want to get ahead of it, grab the latest Apple TV 4K. Although it’s not cheap, it stands out with built-in mics for Siri AI, lots of power, HomePod surround sound support, and a simple, ad-free interface.

    According to recent reports, the Switch 2 leverages the same ideas as its predecessor, only with a larger, 7.9-inch display, a faster chip, and a bevy of upcoming social features. However, its most important trait is that it’s the newest Nintendo console, which means access to a host of weird, beautiful, family-friendly games that only Nintendo could dream up, now on a better screen.

    BougeRV’s fancy, compact lamp will spark joy for the glamper in your life, as well as everyone else. Its powerful, foldable spread of LEDs provides a blast of light anywhere plug-ins can’t reach, from the beach to the shed where that scary spider holds court, with up to 60 hours of light on low power.

    The Rival Pro offers plenty of thoughtful extras, including swappable batteries and an ultra-wideband base station for a seamless, low-latency connection. The gaming mouse’s lightweight design and 8,000Hz polling rate also deliver both accurate and ergonomic performance for up to 16 hours per charge.

    Sources indicate that for the manga or live-action Netflix show lover on your list, this fashionable Pirates jersey, inspired by Monkey D. Luffy from the seminal pirate adventure series One Piece, will be as surprising as it is delightful.

    Zero Manufacturer, a strategy game set in the twilight of the Clone Wars, is a fun way to get lost in the Star Wars universe. The single-player, turn-based title lets players command a diverse team of characters across a gorgeous expanse of worlds, offering hours of solitary entertainment.

    We fell for Apple’s handy iPhone strap due to its effortless accessibility and comfy design, which uses flexible magnets to keep excess segments in check. From biking to hiking to concerts, it’s a great way to sling your iPhone 18 Pro, assuming you have a compatible phone case.

    According to recent reports, the new Fitbit Air provides the same great fitness tracking we’ve come to expect in a comfortable design that virtually disappears on your wrist. Google’s AI Coach can be overly assertive, but the tracker’s great battery life and metrics for everything from sleep to blood oxygen make it an excellent gift for anyone who needs a healthy hand.

    In a recent development, most of us have thousands of photos in the cloud, but if a photo never makes it into the real world, did it really happen? Existentialism aside, the Cricut StickerPix offers a upcoming way to play with photos, providing you with everything you need to turn any picture into a pro-quality print or sticker.

    According to recent reports, this battery-powered fan is a big upgrade over your average plug-in job. As a 3D circulator, it can tilt to push air in all directions. It can be controlled from an app and even detaches from its stand to sit on a desk or tabletop. Quiet, powerful, and versatile, it’s equipped for nearly any adventure on or off the grid.

    Recent findings suggest that if your favorite cinephile is looking to get off the streaming carousel, the Kaleidescape Strato E is the key. The premium player lets library builders locally store and play their favorite films and TV shows in lossless 4K resolution with Dolby Atmos for sterling entertainment that’s all theirs.

    Once The Great British Baking Show becomes an obsession, only a serious stand mixer will do for replicating recipes at home. This mixer’s timeless design adds fresh features in what KitchenAid calls its biggest upgrade since 1955, with a new half-speed setting and a control lever that lets you set speeds between its standard settings.

    The Pocket Scion is unlike any musical instrument you’ve witnessed before, one that uses the “biofeedback” from plants to trigger built-in synths. The device offers MIDI-out to send digital signals to outboard synths, and it includes an app for both macOS and Windows, finally giving you a way to make your favorite fern a rockstar.

    When it comes to jotting down notes, there’s nothing like a pen and paper. At least, that’s what we thought before we tried the Remarkable Paper Pure. Offering a strikingly realistic writing experience that saves everything in the digital realm, this tablet is a brilliant way to bridge the gap and save paper.

    Recent findings suggest that electronics are becoming more sustainable, and Fairphone is leading the way. The Fairphone 6 Plus may seem like a regular Android phone on paper, but the ability to repair and replace its internals, from the screen to the battery, makes it anything but average.

    #105116. Tech Report: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to U.S. industrial might — not a champion

    📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1530 w)
    📖 Baca
    Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to U.S. industrial might — not a champion

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1530 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that investors cheered Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday, but renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale thinks they’re celebrating a mistake.
    • As evidence, Sonnenfeld points to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S.
    • According to recent reports, indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with just as much enthusiasm in Asia, The Washington Post reported.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that investors cheered Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia’s CEO on Monday, but renowned business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of Yale thinks they’re celebrating a mistake. He sees a tech giant that is largely responsible for putting sophisticated technology in the hands of the country’s adversaries, at a moment when the risks couldn’t be higher. Far from a champion of American industry, he indicates, Nvidia is “a detriment to U.S. global industrial might.”.

    As evidence, Sonnenfeld points to research suggesting Nvidia’s most advanced chips have reached China despite U.S. export controls, and to sinking shares of Anthropic, which he links to the realization that China’s seemingly miraculous open-source AI models are, in a sense, copies of top U.S. labs’ work, even as Nvidia has insisted that smuggling is a “non-factor.”.

    According to recent reports, indeed, Huang’s return was greeted with just as much enthusiasm in Asia, The Washington Post reported. “The king is back!” read one headline from China’s state-affiliated Star Market Daily.

    Industry observers note that the reinstatement itself followed heavy pressure from Washington. Nvidia’s chairman had effectively ruled out Huang’s return just last week. Then, in a torrent of private weekend calls led by Vice President JD Vance, top administration officials leaned on the board to welcome Huang back, with President Trump calling the board directly to vouch for him. “I made the deal,” Trump told CNBC on Monday.

    Sonnenfeld says the directors who went along, and who returned Huang to the board even as it investigates whether foreign intelligence efforts targeted him, now face a “historic level of individual liability.”.

    Sources indicate that the legal deluge has already begun. As we noted a couple of weeks ago, a potential class-action lawsuit was filed almost immediately. Days later, a shareholder derivative suit followed. Filed on Nvidia’s behalf against the directors themselves, the suit alleges the board ignored red flags about Huang’s relationship with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang.

    The class action is very much aimed at making Nvidia and Huang compensate investors for their losses, while the derivative suit puts the directors’ own behavior on trial, with any recovery going to Nvidia. Three more suits followed on Nov. 18, the day after Nvidia’s most recent earnings call; all five were filed in Northern California, where Nvidia is based.

    Huang and Nvidia are also juggling a Justice Department antitrust investigation, a reported SEC probe into Nvidia’s accounting, a possible FBI review, a California subpoena, an export-control case that landed partner Megaspeed on the U.S. trade blacklist on Monday, and congressional inquiries, including a Senate Banking hearing next week at which Huang has agreed to testify.

    Here’s more of what Sonnenfeld had to say, in a Q&A that’s been edited for length and clarity.

    TC: So much has happened since we last talked. Huang was ousted, he’s come back. Do you think the board’s reliance on government assurances here is defensible or an abdication of its own duties?

    JS: They failed to rely on experts. That’s one of the reasons this board is going to be sued and lose, and these directors are likely to face a historic level of individual liability. They have a very inadequate directors and officers liability policy. They have also just failed in their diligence. They hired the Wachtell [law] firm. The Wachtell firm barely got off the blocks to do an investigation. And then they have already reversed themselves, so they didn’t use the expertise needed.

    It’s wild that they also put Huang right back on the board of directors.

    The board showed, in addition to incompetence and collaboration, just cowardice in their capitulation because Trump has nothing to wave over them. If this was SpaceX, where 46% of its business comes from the government [you could maybe see the case for Trump’s involvement].For Nvidia, it’s not even 1% of its business that comes from the U.S. government, so [the board] didn’t have that threat. [Trump] can call off [federal] investigations, but he can’t call off the shareholder litigation. Some are already filed, and the estimates are there’ll probably be 30 of them, and they’re going to be extremely costly.

    And this is not, by the way, just a blue or red state matter. We already have 14 GOP senators who’ve already come out against this, and very prominent conservatives, like Pete Ricketts and Josh Hawley and Tom Cotton and John Cornyn. Those are some issues that may help explain why Nvidia’s stock is tumbling today.Might the board say, ‘We saw the classified intelligence findings, and they assure us Jensen will be absolved of wrongdoing’?

    They haven’t seen those findings, and we also haven’t seen what will be the result of the Senate Intelligence Committee, the Senate Special Committee on Investigations, the Senate Banking Committee, and all their House counterparts. The board hasn’t seen any of that, and even if they saw it, which they have not yet, that still wouldn’t matter.

    Do you think the Commerce Department will continue to tighten its chip export controls to keep China from accessing so much compute or walk back some of those recent moves?

    Recent findings suggest that we already see that Megaspeed has finally been put on the sanctions list, as it should have been before. And we have documentation now that Nvidia, rather than a champion of U.S. global industrial might, is actually a detriment to U.S. global industrial might, because their chips have now turned out to be in the hands and in the systems of not just the Chinese military, as they got channeled to Northwestern Polytechnical University, which is a military institution — this is going into weapons that will, of course, be funneled to Iran and Russia, and they didn’t have access to that a year ago. [Editor’s note: China has long denied supplying weapons to either country. Nvidia chips have been found in Russian drones, however, and the U.S. ambassador to China remarked in September that President Trump had discussed selling arms to China, an account Trump has denied.].

    The open-source models that people have celebrated and marveled at — that China somehow has this ingenuity to be creating their own chips, so that Kimi and DeepSeek and these other celebrated open-source models were producing a miracle of Anthropic-like results — turns out we know why. They are pirating it. They are “distilling it” from Anthropic using high-end Nvidia chips.

    Nvidia has denied reports that its most advanced chips have been smuggled into China.

    There’s an Israeli tech giant, Lava, that just three weeks ago showed [dozens of] Blackwell chips are in China. We’re seeing, with the return of Jensen Huang, Anthropic plummet. Why would that be? Of course, this is because it’s hurting OpenAI. It’s hurting Grok. It’s hurting Perplexity. It’s hurting Gemini. And you’ve seen none of these tech titans celebrate this. We have the misogynist tech bros holding locker-room-type rallies about Jensen Huang’s return, but nobody else has spoken out in favor of this. [You’re not hearing from] the CEOs of Microsoft or IBM or J.P. Morgan or Walmart or General Motors or Caterpillar. Nobody thinks that this is a good move.

    You don’t think Nvidia needed Huang back?

    He was not the guy designing the chips. It’s important to point out that that’s a guy named Chris Malachowsky, a co-founder who’s still there who designed these GPUs and has a whole team of next-generation people like Jonah Alben doing the chip design. As for the great software that has leveraged these chips, that’s also not Jensen Huang. That’s a guy named Ian Buck, who’s been very much celebrated in the last two weeks. He’s the one who designed the CUDA software that leverages the chips. Those people weren’t going anywhere, and wherever Jensen Huang is has nothing to do with them.

    Some are trying to make Huang’s forced resignation about the extramarital affairs to which he has admitted, calling it HR policy gone wild.

    A CEO who doesn’t stand by his own code of conduct makes it completely unenforceable.

    Wired quoted an Nvidia employee who remarked they’d never take an HR training course again if Huang was reinstated.

    Industry observers note that this thing is a sexual affair with a subordinate — whether it’s coercion, or even if it truly was somehow consensual, it’s not fair. All the other people on that team rise and fall with a sexual relationship; it’s something they have no control over.

Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday.     Sources indicate that coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.

    FinCEN’s alert comes in the wake of a reported breach of unclassified information at US spy agencies, including the CIA.

    FinCEN’s alert comes in the wake of a reported breach of unclassified information at US spy agencies, including the CIA.

    The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed on Tuesday that it’s investigating a “cybersecurity incident.” The bureau, which is part of the Treasury Department, said it’s looking into an “incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems.” It hasn’t offered any information about the full scope or source of the breach, but FinCEN has taken some systems offline as a precaution.

    The news comes hours after The Newly introduced York Times reported that the Central Intelligence Agency and Office of the Director of National Security discovered a breach of an open source intelligence system, exposing unclassified information. It’s unclear if the FinCEN breach is related. Americans have been on high alert about security incidents after a series of seemingly unrelated outages earlier this month.

    Americans have been on high alert about security incidents.

    In a recent development, finCEN’s role is to protect the financial system from illegal activity, including by combatting money laundering and terrorism financing. The bureau maintains financial transaction data and distributes it for law enforcement purposes. FinCEN also houses reports of suspicious activity that financial institutions file as part of the Bank Secrecy Act.

    FinCEN notes in its alert that banks can still file reports about suspicious activity online, but some services may not be immediately available. Filers that need to expedite their reports in the meantime can still call the Financial Institutions Hotline, which it says was not impacted by the disruption.
